title: Why Do Nails Grow 3mm a Month Forever?
description:
Why do your fingernails keep growing your whole life when your bones stopped growing in your teens? Growth plates in long bones turn to solid bone after puberty, but the nail matrix under your cuticle keeps making new cells, about 3 mm of fingernail a month.

topic: Why do your nails keep growing when your arms stopped?
script: Your nails never stop growing, but your arms stopped years ago. So why does one keep going? It starts with your bones. Near each end of a long bone sits a soft strip called a growth plate. It keeps adding new bone, so your arms get longer. But by your late teens, that strip turns to solid bone. The plate closes, and your arms stop for good. Nails work differently. Under your cuticle hides the nail matrix, a tiny factory that never shuts down. It keeps making new cells, pushing the older ones forward. Those cells harden and die, which is why clipping doesn't hurt. Fingernails grow about three millimeters a month, so a whole new nail takes around six months. So which grows faster: your fingernails, or your toenails?
key_facts: Long bones lengthen at growth plates (epiphyseal plates) near each end
Growth plates ossify and close after puberty, around the late teens
The nail matrix under the cuticle produces new cells throughout life, pushing older ones forward
Nail plate cells harden (keratinize) and are dead, so clipping is painless
Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month; a whole fingernail regrows in about 6 months; toenails grow slower
